title: Single-cell increment returns the observed prior counter as a witness field
asA: developer relying on per-instance FIFO serialisation for a mint or lock-shape operation
iWant: each concurrent increment to return the observed prior-counter as a witness field
soThat: a downstream assertion can prove the second write observed the first without racing against clock

acceptanceCriteria.description: increment() resolves with a {counter, witness} pair where witness equals the counter value at the start of that call's serialised turn. Two concurrent increments starting from 0 report witnesses 0 and 1 (in FIFO order); a subsequent read reports counter 2. The witness field is present on every resolved increment, never on read or reset.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the FIFO-first increment returns witness 0, the second returns witness 1, and read returns 2

acceptanceCriteria.description: read() has no witness field: a SingleCellObject at counter 3 driven with read() resolves to a bare number 3, not an object; there is no witness field on a read result. The witness is a per-increment observable, tied to serialisation, and does not apply to a pure read that does not advance the FIFO queue.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the result is the primitive number 3 (no witness field, no object wrapping)

acceptanceCriteria.description: reset() has no witness field: a reset() call against a SingleCellObject at counter 5 resolves to the primitive number 0 (the reset value); no witness field. reset advances the FIFO turn but its return contract mirrors read, not increment.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the result is the primitive number 0 (no witness field)

acceptanceCriteria.description: N=100 concurrent increments: 100 concurrent increment(1) calls at initial counter 0 resolve to 100 {counter, witness} pairs. Sorted witnesses equal [0..99] exactly (no gaps, no duplicates); sorted counters equal [1..100]. read() after the batch returns 100. The FIFO queue holds under high concurrency.
acceptanceCriteria.when: 100 concurrent increment(1) calls fire and read follows
acceptanceCriteria.then: sorted witnesses equal [0..99]; sorted counters equal [1..100]; read returns 100
